reviews.title: Review is for the product itself and not the vendor
reviews.comment:
The card is a beast.  Most people already know this though.  It's BIG in size too.  Make sure to measure your case first.  It runs exceptionally cool as well.  I've OC'd the GPU to 3000 keeping fans at 100% and constant load temps hit around 55c max.  That's actually cooler (by a couple degrees) than my 3090Ti on a 360mm radiator under full load!
Not going to bash the vendor as it was my choice to buy at the inflated pricing.  I figured if I wanted to get it by Christmas this was the only option.
It's a shame EVGA is still not in the Nvidia market as they had a pretty good sales system to help keep the scalpers at bay and get the cards into the hands of consumers at MSRP.  It's too bad the other manufacturers have not done something similar.
Anyway, this so far has been a great card!  I really like the looks and performance of it.

reviews.title: So heavy that the card bends with the included support bracket...
reviews.comment:
I'm a veteran system builder with at least 1,000 desktop system builds under my belt, so it's always interesting to find quirks in new generations of hardware. The Aorus Master GeForce 4090 definitely has some quirks. Namely, upon installation of the device with the included support bracket, the weight of the heatsink is so great that the top metal plate actually bent between the PCI-E slot and support bracket when the tower case was gently raised to its vertical position. So, there's a defect / oversight right there.
The fan spin up isn't always consistent, with some fans lighting and spinning up and down at slightly different rates from others, regardless of how the fan curve is set in the Gigabyte app. This isn't super annoying or concerning, but it is a little odd how much of a delay there can be between them.
Having only used the provided presets in the Gigabyte app for the GPU's screen, they seem to work pretty well, but I have yet to try a custom image or gif.
The three displayports (not using the most current standard) and single current standard HDMI port was a strange choice, especially with more and more devices seeming to lean towards HDMI. Every port on this card SHOULD support 8k at 120 Hz, but doesn't for... Reasons? Considering this is a $1800 luxury product, it should do that and more.
Using latest drivers and default settings, the Aorus Master 4090 paired with a 7950X3D on the Aorus Master motherboard posted pretty middle of the road scores in futuremark for 4090 class GPUs, which was a little disappointing, but within expectations.
As is the case of ALL the high-end 40 series cards, these are a terrible value and an obvious money grab from NVIDIA. This card went in a new build that replaced my (still very capable) GeForce 1080 from six years ago which, ironically, has a better set of connection options than the new card that costs around four times as much.
The proprietary NVIDIA cable is also an eyesore that will require additional parts if aesthetics are paramount to your build.
It is, however, the most powerful graphics chip on the market paired with a beefy cooler, and I hope it will last a long time... Even though I probably should request an RMA over the defective plate attachment points.
Please note; the radiator tubes ideally would be going to the bottom of the radiator, but case limitations prevented such an orientation.
